name: Learn basic beatboxing
blurb: Three sounds — kick, hi-hat, snare — and you have a beat. Everything else in beatboxing is built on those three and the ability to breathe while patterning.
steps: Learn the kick drum: a hard, lipped “b” sound with no vowel, driven by a burst of air from the diaphragm.
Learn the closed hi-hat: a short “t” or “ts”, crisp and quiet.
Learn the classic snare: the “pf” rim shot to start, then progress to the harder “k” snare.
Combine into the basic pattern: boom, ts, pf, ts, repeated. Say it slowly, then speed it up.
Learn to breathe through the pattern — inhaling on a hi-hat is the standard trick.
Add variation: rolls, double kicks, and a hummed bassline underneath.
tips: Speed comes last. Get the pattern clean at half tempo first.
Cup your hands around your mouth and a phone microphone to hear what an audience hears.
proof: A continuous 60-second beat with a steady tempo, breathing without breaking the pattern.
